claims.text: Atom probe tomography can elucidate oxidation-induced elemental redistribution in nanoprecipitates of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
Preferential oxidation of specific elements at nanoprecipitate interfaces plays a key role in the alloy's oxidation behavior.
The initial material is an additively manufactured dual-nanoprecipitation Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy.
High-temperature oxidative exposure induces changes at nanoprecipitates and their interfaces with the matrix.
APT will reveal elemental-composition gradients at nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces.
Al, Ti, or other oxidation-prone elements will segregate at nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces.
Interfacial compositional variations mediate the formation and stability of protective oxide layers.
Stable protective oxide layers improve oxidation resistance.
APT measurements will show distinct elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitate boundaries.
Certain elements will concentrate at nanoprecipitate boundaries to form coherent oxide layers.
Interfacial elemental segregation will correlate with improved oxidation resistance relative to cast or wrought samples.
Cast and wrought forms of the same alloy lack the nanostructural refinement achieved by additive manufacturing.
The proposed observations may not apply to other degradation mechanisms or substantially different temperature regimes.
TEM-EDS can provide complementary validation of APT observations.
